sections.subtitle: Sub Club otvara razgovor o učenju jezika, temi koja je bliska i voditeljima
sections.screenshot_description: Voditelj David pozdravlja gosta Adama Turaeva i suvoditelja Jacoba na početku epizode
sections.content:
Epizoda podcasta **Sub Club** počinje uobičajenom najavom. Emisija je posvećena najboljim praksama u gradnji i rastu poslovanja temeljenog na aplikacijama. Voditelji razgovaraju s poduzetnicima, investitorima i graditeljima koji stoje iza nekih od najuspješnijih aplikacija na svijetu kako bi učili iz njihovih uspjeha i neuspjeha. Voditelj David podsjeća da emisiju omogućuje **RevenueCat**, kojemu tisuće aplikacija prepuštaju kupnje unutar aplikacije, upravljanje korisnicima i rast prihoda na iOS-u, Androidu i webu.

Nakon uvoda David pozdravlja gosta, **Adama Turaeva**, jednog od osnivača aplikacije Praktika, te suvoditelja **Jacoba**, izvršnog direktora RevenueCata. Jacob odmah kaže da se veseli razgovoru jer spaja dvije njegove omiljene teme: učenje jezika i aplikacije.

David otkriva da je Jacob dugogodišnji učenik stranih jezika, pa mu je tema epizode posebno bliska. Jacob uz osmijeh priznaje da je trenutačno na pauzi. David primjećuje da je to razumljivo jer je ipak izvršni direktor RevenueCata, a Jacob potvrđuje da ga taj posao drži zauzetim. Dodaje da jezike voli učiti i kao zabavni „trik za zabave”. Ta će razlika između učenja jezika iz razonode i učenja iz nužde postati jedna od glavnih niti cijelog razgovora.
sections.subtitle_en: Sub Club Opens the Conversation on Language Learning, a Topic Close to the Hosts as Well
sections.screenshot_description_en: Host David Welcomes Guest Adam Turaev and Co-Host Jacob at the Beginning of the Episode
sections.content_en:
The episode of the **Sub Club** podcast begins with the usual announcement. The show is dedicated to best practices in building and growing an app-based business. The hosts speak with entrepreneurs, investors, and builders behind some of the most successful applications in the world in order to learn from their successes and failures. Host David reminds that the show is made possible by **RevenueCat**, to which thousands of applications outsource in-app purchases, subscriber management, and revenue growth on iOS, Android, and web.

After the introduction, David welcomes the guest, **Adam Turaev**, one of the founders of the Praktika app, and co-host **Jacob**, CEO of RevenueCat. Jacob immediately says he looks forward to the conversation because it combines two of his favorite topics: language learning and apps.

David reveals that Jacob is a longtime foreign language learner, so the episode's topic is especially close to him. Jacob smilingly admits that he is currently taking a break. David remarks that this is understandable since he is, after all, the CEO of RevenueCat, and Jacob confirms that the job keeps him busy. He adds that he also likes to learn languages as a fun “party trick.” That difference between learning a language for leisure and learning out of necessity will become one of the main threads of the entire conversation.

sections.subtitle: Od chatbotova za korporacije do vlastite boli: kako je nastala Praktika
sections.screenshot_description: Adam Turaev objašnjava kako je CleverBots automatizirao do 60 posto korisničkih upita za velike tvrtke
sections.content:
David otvara razgovor pitanjem o zaokretu. Adam se prije Praktike bavio chatbotovima za velike tvrtke u kompaniji **CleverBots**. David ga pita zašto je prešao u potrošačko učenje jezika i zašto je ušao u tržište na kojem dominira Duolingo, „gorila od 400 kilograma” s kojom se, prema općem uvjerenju, nitko ne bi trebao natjecati.

Adam objašnjava da su on i suosnivači, **Anton i Ilya**, školski prijatelji. Godinama su zajedno radili projekte i sanjali o nečemu inovativnom što bi donijelo vrijednost ljudima diljem svijeta. Problema koje vrijedi riješiti ima mnogo, ali jedan su osobno proživjeli: **jezičnu barijeru**.

Istodobno su duboko ušli u **konverzacijsku umjetnu inteligenciju**. Tražili su način da njome pomognu korporativnim klijentima i tako je 2017. nastao CleverBots, dugo prije ere velikih jezičnih modela. Jacob primjećuje da je to iste godine kada je objavljen znanstveni rad o **Transformer** arhitekturi. Adam dodaje da se tada govorilo o obradi prirodnog jezika (NLP), a ne o LLM-ovima.

Jedna od prvih inspiracija bio je **Pavel Durov**, kada je **Telegram** otvorio API za chatbotove. Jacob podsjeća na val chatbotova sredinom prošlog desetljeća, prije LLM-ova. Facebook ih je snažno gurao, svi su mislili da je proboj na pragu, a onda se to nikada nije dogodilo.

Adamova dugoročna vizija bila je da će upravo tako ljudi komunicirati sa strojevima. CleverBots je radio s najvećim međunarodnim kompanijama i nudio chatbotove i glasovna rješenja:
- automatizirali su **korisničku podršku**,
- preuzeli su dio **HR podrške**,
- rješavali su velik broj upita, ponekad i **do 60 posto**, i to prije ere LLM-ova.

Što su dulje radili s tom tehnologijom, to su jasnije vidjeli da ona može riješiti i njihov vlastiti problem. Adam ističe da nije izvorni govornik engleskog, a engleski je za njega **multiplikator prihoda i prilika**. Shvatili su da konverzacijska umjetna inteligencija tu ima mnogo veći potencijal. Odluku o prelasku s CleverBotsa na Praktiku, naglašava, donijeli su još prije ere LLM-ova.
sections.subtitle_en: From Enterprise Chatbots to Their Own Pain: How Praktika Came to Be
sections.screenshot_description_en: Adam Turaev Explains How CleverBots Automated Up to 60 Percent of Customer Inquiries for Large Companies
sections.content_en:
David opens the conversation with a question about the pivot. Before Praktika, Adam worked on chatbots for large companies at **CleverBots**. David asks him why he transitioned into consumer language learning and why he entered a market dominated by Duolingo, the “400-pound gorilla” with which, according to conventional wisdom, no one should compete.

Adam explains that he and co-founders, **Anton and Ilya**, are school friends. For years they worked on projects together and dreamed of something innovative that would bring value to people worldwide. There are many problems worth solving, but they experienced one personally: the **language barrier**.

At the same time, they went deep into **conversational artificial intelligence**. They were looking for a way to use it to help corporate clients, and so in 2017 CleverBots was born, long before the era of large language models. Jacob notes that this was the same year the research paper on the **Transformer** architecture was published. Adam adds that at that time people spoke of natural language processing (NLP), not LLMs.

One of the early inspirations was **Pavel Durov**, when **Telegram** opened its API for chatbots. Jacob recalls the chatbot wave in the middle of the last decade, before LLMs. Facebook pushed them aggressively, everyone thought a breakthrough was around the corner, and then it never happened.

Adam's long-term vision was that this was precisely how humans would communicate with machines. CleverBots worked with top international companies and offered chatbots and voice solutions:
- they automated **customer support**,
- they took over part of **HR support**,
- they handled a large number of inquiries, sometimes **up to 60 percent**, and that was before the LLM era.

The longer they worked with that technology, the more clearly they saw that it could also solve their own problem. Adam emphasizes that he is not a native English speaker, and for him English is an **income and opportunity multiplier**. They realized that conversational artificial intelligence had far greater potential there. The decision to transition from CleverBots to Praktika, he emphasizes, was made even before the era of LLMs.

sections.subtitle: Prerano, ali s potpunim uvjerenjem: prototipi od 2021. i vjera u sazrijevanje modela
sections.screenshot_description: Jacob pita Adama je li vjerovao da će modeli postati bolji, a Adam odgovara da je bio stopostotno uvjeren
sections.content:
David primjećuje da je ovo priča u kojoj je osnivač imao pravo, ali s tajmingom koji nije sjeo. Da je CleverBots pokrenut oko 2020. ili 2021., bio bi u izvrsnoj poziciji kada su stigli LLM-ovi. Zanima ga je li se sa zaokretom prema Praktiki dogodilo nešto slično, odnosno je li tvrtka jednostavno uhvatila val LLM-ova, samo u učenju jezika.

Adam kaže da je Praktika javno pokrenuta 2024., ali je put mnogo dulji. O ideji i primjeni konverzacijske umjetne inteligencije počeli su razmišljati još 2021. i tada su izradili prve prototipove, koje sam opisuje kao „prilično loše”. Jacob se pita kada je izašao prvi GPT API i misli da je to bilo 2022. Adam smatra da je bilo otprilike u to vrijeme i sjeća se da su ga koristili. Jacob dodaje da su ti rani modeli bili toliko nepouzdani da se s njima zapravo nije mogao voditi razgovor.

Na Jacobovo pitanje je li jednostavno vjerovao da će se tehnologija skalirati i poboljšati, Adam odgovara bez oklijevanja: **stopostotno uvjerenje**. Priznaje da je to danas lako reći. Jacob duhovito dodaje da Adam, da se stvar razvila drukčije, sada ne bi sjedio u podcastu, a David to naziva **pristranošću preživjelih**.

Jacob priznaje da je dan ranije o tome pisao na Twitteru jer je, kako kaže, cijelo vrijeme podcjenjivao ove tehnologije i smatrao ih zanimljivim novitetima. Oni koji su vjerovali prije nego što je to postalo mainstream morali su imati mnogo uvjerenja da ustraju i ulažu iako modeli još nisu bili spremni.

Adam podsjeća da je to bilo vrijeme kada su svi bili opsjednuti **Web 3.0**. CleverBots je tada nudio automatizaciju chatbotovima i oko nje je bilo mnogo obećanja, ali su klijenti od tadašnjih chatbotova očekivali ono što mogu današnji. Zato je tajming bio pomaknut. Tim je ipak znao da je samo pitanje vremena kada će tehnologija sazrjeti, a upravo im je to rano uvjerenje omogućilo da budu među prvima koji su se uhvatili baš ovog problema.
sections.subtitle_en: Too Early, but with Complete Conviction: Prototypes from 2021 and Faith in Model Maturation
sections.screenshot_description_en: Jacob Asks Adam Whether He Believed the Models Would Get Better, and Adam Answers That He Was One Hundred Percent Convinced
sections.content_en:
David remarks that this is a story where the founder was right, but with timing that did not click. Had CleverBots been launched around 2020 or 2021, it would have been in an excellent position when LLMs arrived. He wonders whether something similar happened with the pivot to Praktika, that is, whether the company simply caught the LLM wave, only in language learning.

Adam says that Praktika was launched publicly in 2024, but the journey was much longer. They started thinking about the idea and application of conversational artificial intelligence back in 2021, and that is when they built the first prototypes, which he himself describes as “pretty bad.” Jacob wonders when the first GPT API came out and thinks it was in 2022. Adam thinks it was around that time and remembers that they used it. Jacob adds that those early models were so unreliable that one could not actually hold a conversation with them.

To Jacob's question of whether he simply believed that the technology would scale and improve, Adam answers without hesitation: **one hundred percent conviction**. He admits that today this is easy to say. Jacob wittily adds that had things unfolded differently, Adam would not be sitting on the podcast right now, and David calls this **survivorship bias**.

Jacob admits that the day before he wrote about this on Twitter because, as he says, he underestimated these technologies the entire time and viewed them as interesting novelties. Those who believed before it became mainstream had to have a lot of conviction to persevere and invest even though the models were not yet ready.

Adam recalls that this was the time when everyone was obsessed with **Web 3.0**. CleverBots was offering chatbot automation back then and there was a lot of promise around it, but clients expected from the chatbots of that time what today's chatbots can do. That is why the timing was off. The team still knew that it was only a matter of time before the technology matured, and precisely that early conviction allowed them to be among the first to tackle this exact problem.

sections.subtitle: Stotine chatbotova kao škola: zašto tim zna kako se korisnici ponašaju u razgovoru sa strojem
sections.screenshot_description: Adam Turaev govori o konverzacijskom korisničkom iskustvu i trenucima kada korisnici odustaju
sections.content:
Jacob ističe još jednu prednost ranog starta: tim je jednostavno naučio graditi s ovim alatima. Kaže da je RevenueCat tu lekciju naučio ove godine. Tvrtka je kaskala jer nije bila prisiljena učiti te alate, a sada sustiže zaostatak u **agentnom inženjerstvu** i radu s API-jima modela. Godine iskustva s takvim alatima, smatra Jacob, prava su prednost.

Adam se nadovezuje i opisuje cijelo zasebno područje, **konverzacijsko korisničko iskustvo**. Riječ je o tome kako ljudi očekuju da chatbot reagira i odgovara te u kojim trenucima odustaju. Te su temeljne obrasce u CleverBotsu upoznali gradeći stotine chatbotova, još u eri prije LLM-ova. Zahvaljujući tome tim je, kako kaže, imao vrlo jasne stavove o tome što gradi.
sections.subtitle_en: Hundreds of Chatbots as a School: Why the Team Knows How Users Behave in Conversation with a Machine
sections.screenshot_description_en: Adam Turaev Speaks About Conversational User Experience and the Moments When Users Drop Off
sections.content_en:
Jacob highlights another advantage of an early start: the team simply learned to build with these tools. He says RevenueCat learned that lesson this year. The company lagged behind because it was not forced to learn those tools, and now it is catching up in **agentic engineering** and working with model APIs. Years of experience with such tools, Jacob believes, are a real advantage.

Adam follows up and describes an entire distinct field, **conversational user experience**. It is about how people expect a chatbot to react and respond, and at what moments they give up. They learned these fundamental patterns at CleverBots by building hundreds of chatbots, back in the pre-LLM era. Thanks to that, the team, as he says, had very clear opinions on what they were building.

sections.subtitle: Rješavati vlastiti problem, a ne loviti najveće tržište
sections.screenshot_description: Adam Turaev objašnjava da zaokret nije bio motiviran veličinom tržišta nego stvarnim problemom
sections.content:
David želi više detalja o samom zaokretu. Smatra da bi mnogi osnivači trebali promijeniti smjer, bilo zato što stvari ne funkcioniraju ili zato što negdje drugdje postoji veća prilika. Zato pita kako je odluka donesena, kako je izgledao prijelaz, što se dogodilo sa starom tvrtkom i jesu li u obje kompanije prikupljali novac od istih investitora.

Adam se u odgovoru ne bavi financiranjem, nego motivacijom. Presudna je, kaže, bila iskrena želja da riješe problem koji poznaju i znanje da ga konverzacijska umjetna inteligencija može riješiti. Nisu tražili gdje je najveće ukupno adresabilno tržište.

Presudni su bili sljedeći uvidi:
- problem stvarno postoji,
- korisnici su nezadovoljni postojećim rješenjima,
- nitko nije nudio takvo rješenje, što im je bilo, kako kaže, „prilično tužno” vidjeti.

Kada su shvatili da takvog rješenja nema, krenuli su. Znali su da je tržište veliko, ali Adam priznaje da nisu očekivali da će biti toliko veliko.
sections.subtitle_en: Solving One's Own Problem Rather Than Chasing the Biggest Market
sections.screenshot_description_en: Adam Turaev Explains That the Pivot Was Not Motivated by Market Size but by a Real Problem
sections.content_en:
David wants more details about the pivot itself. He believes that many founders should change direction, either because things are not working or because there is a bigger opportunity elsewhere. Therefore, he asks how the decision was made, what the transition looked like, what happened to the old company, and whether they raised money from the same investors in both companies.

In his response, Adam does not address financing, but motivation. The decisive factor, he says, was a genuine desire to solve a problem they knew and the knowledge that conversational artificial intelligence could solve it. They were not looking for where the largest total addressable market was.

The decisive factors were the following insights:
- the problem really exists,
- users are dissatisfied with existing solutions,
- no one was offering such a solution, which was, as he says, “pretty sad” for them to see.

When they realized that there was no such solution, they went for it. They knew the market was large, but Adam admits they did not expect it to be so large.

sections.subtitle: Engleski za karijeru umjesto edukativne zabave: zašto je Brazil postao ključno tržište
sections.screenshot_description: Adam Turaev objašnjava kako su podaci o poznavanju engleskog doveli Praktiku do Brazila
sections.content:
David ističe da se Praktika usmjerila na **engleski za karijeru i tražitelje posla**, dok je Duolingo opušteniji proizvod, bliži edukativnoj zabavi. To vidi kao klasičan primjer diferencijacije: ulazak na prenapučeno tržište kojeg bi se mnogi klonili, ali s jasno drukčijim pristupom.

Adam prvo odaje priznanje konkurentu. Duolingo je izgradio sjajan proizvod i brojke to i dalje potvrđuju. Jacob ga naziva možda prvom i jedinom obrazovnom aplikacijom golemih razmjera i „generacijskim brendom” koji traje. Adam se slaže da je Duolingo u svojoj ligi, a Praktika ga sustiže. Jacob se šali da im za to treba ptica, odnosno neka vrsta „poludjelog” avatara i čudnih reklama. Adam odgovara da će o tome razgovarati kasnije i da im to vjerojatno ne treba. Jacob ipak priznaje da je Duolingu taj pristup očito upalio.

Adam objašnjava da je polazište ponovno bio njihov vlastiti problem. Kroz iskustvo selidbe u druge zemlje shvatili su koliko je teško doista naučiti engleski i probiti **barijeru tečnosti**. Zato su proizvod namijenili ljudima poput sebe.

Izbor tržišta bio je pritom vrlo utemeljen na podacima. Proučili su izvještaj **English First** o poznavanju engleskog jezika i uočili:
- da je **Brazil** jedno od tržišta s najslabijim poznavanjem engleskog,
- da je engleski u takvim zemljama golem **multiplikator prihoda**,
- da je važna i **globalna mobilnost**,
- da ljudi engleski već aktivno uče.

Jacob dodaje da je riječ i o velikoj zemlji sa stotinama milijuna stanovnika. Adam priznaje i bojazan: kupovna moć nije visoka, a Brazilci obično ne plaćaju potrošačke pretplate. Jacob primjećuje da bi upravo to neki drugi tim navelo da tržište zanemari, iako odluka može biti ispravna ako su temelji dobri. Adam zaključuje da su postojali svi preduvjeti za uspjeh i da je procjena bila kako su najraniji korisnici vjerojatno upravo ondje.

Na Jacobovo pitanje je li aplikacija pokrenuta samo u Brazilu, Adam odgovara da je objavljena globalno, bez ograničenja, ali je distribucija bila usmjerena na Brazil. U ponudi je bio isključivo engleski jer su gradili proizvod za ljude poput sebe i za problem koji su sami proživjeli.
sections.subtitle_en: English for Career Instead of Edutainment: Why Brazil Became a Key Market
sections.screenshot_description_en: Adam Turaev Explains How Data on English Proficiency Led Praktika to Brazil
sections.content_en:
David points out that Praktika focused on **English for careers and job seekers**, whereas Duolingo is a more casual product, closer to edutainment. He sees this as a classic example of differentiation: entering a crowded market that many would avoid, but with a clearly distinct approach.

Adam first gives credit to the competitor. Duolingo has built a great product, and the numbers continue to confirm that. Jacob calls it perhaps the first and only educational app of massive scale and a lasting “generational brand.” Adam agrees that Duolingo is in a league of its own, and Praktika is catching up to it. Jacob jokes that for that they need a bird, that is, some kind of “unhinged” avatar and weird ads. Adam replies that they will talk about that later and that they probably do not need it. Jacob nevertheless admits that this approach clearly worked for Duolingo.

Adam explains that the starting point was once again their own problem. Through the experience of moving to other countries, they realized how difficult it is to truly learn English and break through the **fluency barrier**. That is why they designed the product for people like themselves.

The choice of market was, at the same time, highly data-driven. They studied the **English First** report on English language proficiency and noticed:
- that **Brazil** is one of the markets with the lowest English proficiency,
- that English in such countries is a huge **income multiplier**,
- that **global mobility** is also important,
- that people are already actively learning English.

Jacob adds that it is also a large country with hundreds of millions of inhabitants. Adam also admits a concern: purchasing power is not high, and Brazilians usually do not pay for consumer subscriptions. Jacob remarks that precisely this would lead another team to ignore the market, even though the decision may be right if the fundamentals are good. Adam concludes that all the preconditions for success existed and that the assessment was that the earliest users were probably right there.

To Jacob's question of whether the app was launched only in Brazil, Adam replies that it was released globally, without restrictions, but distribution was targeted at Brazil. The offering consisted exclusively of English because they were building a product for people like themselves and for a problem they personally experienced.

sections.subtitle: Ne prodaje se jezik, nego bolji posao: kako je nastala poruka o 50 puta jeftinijem tutoru
sections.screenshot_description: Adam Turaev objašnjava da Praktika korisnicima nije prodavala engleski nego priliku za bolji posao
sections.content:
Jacob citira poznatu maksimu da treba graditi nešto što ljudi žele, a dodaje da je još bolje graditi nešto što ljudima treba. Kada učenje engleskog donosi velik ekonomski dobitak, potreba je stvarna. U obrnutom smjeru to često ne vrijedi. Uz ogradu da generalizira, kaže da je izvornim govornicima engleskog učenje drugog jezika uglavnom luksuz ili hobi.

Adam tada otkriva podrijetlo poruke koju danas koriste mnogi u industriji: **„50 puta jeftinije od tutora”**. Ta je tvrdnja nastala iz strategije izlaska Praktike na brazilsko tržište. Budući da kupovna moć nije visoka, korisnicima je trebalo vrlo jasno objasniti zašto se isplati platiti **100 dolara za godišnju pretplatu** i dobiti tutora uz kojeg mogu napredovati i doći do boljeg posla.

Ključ je bio u promjeni kuta. Praktika korisnicima nije prodavala engleski, nego **priliku za bolji posao**. Sve marketinške poruke bile su građene oko toga, a ne oko obećanja da će netko bolje govoriti engleski. Jacob primjećuje da se reklame koje on viđa vjerojatno jako razlikuju od onih koje vide korisnici u Brazilu, što Adam potvrđuje.

David iz toga izvodi pouku za slušatelje: tko traži problem koji vrijedi riješiti, neka traži onaj u kojem zapravo prodaje novac. Jacob ide korak dalje i tvrdi da postoje samo dvije vrste problema koje se rješavaju za potrošače:
- pomoći im da se obogate,
- pomoći im da novac koji imaju potroše na nešto što ih veseli,
- a možda i treća, ostati zdrav.

Prema njegovim zapažanjima među klijentima RevenueCata, proizvod koji ljudima pomaže zaraditi lakše se prodaje, osobito kada je veza toliko izravna kao napredak u karijeri. Adam to naziva gotovo trivijalnom mišlju: korisnicima treba prodati ono što im na kraju doista treba. Dodaje da se to tijekom gradnje proizvoda stalno zaboravlja.
sections.subtitle_en: Not Selling the Language, but a Better Job: How the Message of 50 Times Cheaper Than a Tutor Came to Be
sections.screenshot_description_en: Adam Turaev Explains That Praktika Did Not Sell English to Users but the Opportunity for a Better Job
sections.content_en:
Jacob cites the well-known maxim that one should build something people want, and adds that it is even better to build something people need. When learning English brings a large economic gain, the need is real. In the opposite direction, that is often not the case. With the caveat that he is generalizing, he says that for native English speakers, learning a second language is mostly a luxury or a hobby.

Adam then reveals the origin of the message used today by many in the industry: **“50 times cheaper than a tutor”**. That claim originated from Praktika's go-to-market strategy for the Brazilian market. Because purchasing power is not high, users needed a very clear explanation of why it pays to pay **100 dollars for an annual subscription** and get a tutor alongside whom they can advance and reach a better job.

The key was in changing the angle. Praktika did not sell English to users, but an **opportunity for a better job**. All marketing messages were built around that, and not around the promise that someone would speak better English. Jacob remarks that the ads he sees probably differ greatly from those seen by users in Brazil, which Adam confirms.

David draws a lesson from this for listeners: whoever is looking for a problem worth solving should look for one where they are actually selling money. Jacob goes a step further and asserts that there are only two types of problems being solved for consumers:
- helping them get rich,
- helping them spend the money they have on something that makes them happy,
- and perhaps a third, staying healthy.

According to his observations among RevenueCat clients, a product that helps people make money sells more easily, especially when the connection is as direct as career advancement. Adam calls this an almost trivial thought: users should be sold what they ultimately really need. He adds that during product development, this is constantly forgotten.

sections.subtitle: Synthesia avatari i stotine ručno pisanih stabala razgovora
sections.screenshot_description: Adam Turaev opisuje rane web verzije Praktike sa Synthesia avatarima i ručno izgrađenim stablima razgovora
sections.content:
Jacob primjećuje da u samom proizvodu vjerojatno nema mnogo govora o traženju posla jer je fokus na učenju jezika. Zatim pita kada se aplikacija prvi put pojavila u App Storeu. Adam odgovara da je to bilo **sredinom 2023.** i odmah dodaje da je to bila „užasna verzija”.

Jacob podsjeća da je tim počeo raditi 2021., kada praktički nije bilo LLM-ova, a ni 2023. s ChatGPT-jem 4 nije bilo mnogo zrelije, osobito kod glasovnih modela. Pretpostavlja da je Praktika imala snažan vjetar u leđa zahvaljujući napretku modela. Pita je li tada bilo moguće postići željenu kvalitetu.

Adam otkriva da je i prije toga, 2022., postojalo nekoliko web verzija. Zbog tehnoloških ograničenja sustav je izgledao ovako:
- kao lice proizvoda služio je **avatar tvrtke Synthesia**, koja je tada već postojala,
- ti avatari nisu radili uživo, a NLP je bio daleko od današnjih LLM-ova,
- zato je tim morao **ručno izgraditi stotine stabala razgovora** koja pokrivaju sve smjerove u kojima se razgovor može razviti.

Jacob primjećuje da je to bilo prije nego što su agenti za programiranje postali dobri, pa je posla bilo još više. Adam potvrđuje da su stabla gradili copywriteri i kreatori sadržaja kako bi iskustvo barem djelovalo kao današnje.

Adam ističe zanimljivu pojedinost: i s takvim ograničenim sustavom tim je inzistirao na **prisutnosti avatara**. Synthesia avatar reagirao je i odgovarao korisniku kako bi se stvorio dojam stvarnog razgovora. Ta će se odluka pokazati kao jedna od temeljnih značajki proizvoda.
sections.subtitle_en: Synthesia Avatars and Hundreds of Hand-Written Conversation Trees
sections.screenshot_description_en: Adam Turaev Describes Early Web Versions of Praktika with Synthesia Avatars and Hand-Built Conversation Trees
sections.content_en:
Jacob remarks that in the product itself there is probably not much talk about job searching because the focus is on language learning. Then he asks when the app first appeared in the App Store. Adam replies that it was **mid-2023** and immediately adds that it was a “terrible version.”

Jacob recalls that the team started working in 2021, when there were practically no LLMs, and even in 2023 with ChatGPT 4 it was not much more mature, especially with voice models. He assumes that Praktika had a strong tailwind thanks to the advancement of models. He asks whether it was possible back then to achieve the desired quality.

Adam reveals that even before that, in 2022, there were several web versions. Due to technological limitations, the system looked like this:
- an **avatar from the company Synthesia**, which already existed at the time, served as the face of the product,
- those avatars did not work live, and NLP was far from today's LLMs,
- that is why the team had to **manually build hundreds of conversation trees** covering all directions in which a conversation could develop.

Jacob remarks that this was before coding agents became good, so there was even more work. Adam confirms that the trees were built by copywriters and content creators so that the experience would at least feel like today's.

Adam highlights an interesting detail: even with such a limited system, the team insisted on the **presence of an avatar**. The Synthesia avatar reacted and responded to the user in order to create the impression of a real conversation. That decision would prove to be one of the fundamental features of the product.

sections.subtitle: Gradnja na rubu tehnologije i znanje o korisnicima koje modeli nemaju
sections.screenshot_description: Adam Turaev govori o tome kako Anthropic i OpenAI danas potiču gradnju na rubu tehnologije
sections.content:
David iz toga izvlači još jednu lekciju i priznaje vlastitu pogrešnu procjenu, baš kao ranije Jacob. U ranim danima **Midjourneyja** napisao je na Twitteru da će s generiranjem slika biti kao sa samovozećim automobilima: činit će se da je proboj blizu, a trajat će još desetljeće. Pokazalo se da nije trebalo desetljeće. Za oko dvije godine Midjourney je od slika sa šest prstiju došao do nevjerojatno fotorealističnih prikaza. Tko je uvjeren da će tehnologija sustići viziju, zaključuje David, gradi ono što može danas, uz mnogo napornog rada.

Adam primjećuje da je takvo uvjerenje danas lako imati, dok je tada bilo kontroverzno. Sada i **Anthropic** i **OpenAI** otvoreno poručuju da treba graditi na rubu tehnoloških mogućnosti, a svaki novi model potvrđuje da će tehnologija sustići.

Jacob se slaže da to više nije oklada protiv konsenzusa, ali naglašava da je trebalo biti rano. Među današnjim pobjednicima u raznim područjima mnogo je tvrtki koje nisu bile prerano, ali su bile dovoljno rano, vjerovale su i pametno su uložile da uhvate val. Ne tvrdi da je sada prekasno, ali sposobnost da se razdoblje čekanja izdrži bila je velika prednost.

Odvaja zatim dva sastojka dobrog proizvoda. Prvi su sami modeli. Spominje razgovor izvan snimanja o tome kako su glasovni modeli već prilično dobri u razgovoru na drugim jezicima, što je dostupno svima, pa se temeljni modeli na neki način natječu sa svima. Drugi sastojak su **lekcije, razumijevanje korisnika i sve ono čemu modeli imaju tek ograničen pristup**. To se moglo graditi i dok tehnologija još nije bila spremna. Između 2022. i 2024. Praktika je otkrivala što ljudi žele koristiti i kako doći do tržišta, a to se, kaže Jacob, ne može izvući iz modela.

Adam to potvrđuje anegdotom. Tim je snimao sve rane razgovore s korisnicima i i dalje ima stotine intervjua iz 2022. Zanimljivo je, kaže, da ljudi u njima govore potpuno iste stvari kao i u današnjim intervjuima.
sections.subtitle_en: Building on the Frontier of Technology and User Knowledge That Models Lack
sections.screenshot_description_en: Adam Turaev Speaks About How Anthropic and OpenAI Encourage Building on the Frontier of Technology Today
sections.content_en:
David draws another lesson from this and admits his own misjudgment, just like Jacob earlier. In the early days of **Midjourney**, he wrote on Twitter that image generation would be like self-driving cars: a breakthrough would seem close, but it would take another decade. It turned out it did not take a decade. In about two years, Midjourney went from images with six fingers to incredibly photorealistic renders. Whoever is convinced that technology will catch up with the vision, David concludes, builds what they can today, with a lot of hard work.

Adam remarks that such conviction is easy to have today, whereas back then it was controversial. Now both **Anthropic** and **OpenAI** openly say that one should build on the frontier of technological possibilities, and every new model confirms that technology will catch up.

Jacob agrees that this is no longer a non-consensus bet, but emphasizes that one had to be early. Among today's winners across various fields are many companies that were not too early, but were early enough, believed, and invested wisely to catch the wave. He does not claim that it is now too late, but the ability to endure the waiting period was a huge advantage.

He then separates two ingredients of a good product. The first is the models themselves. He mentions an off-the-record conversation about how voice models are already pretty good at conversing in other languages, which is available to everyone, so foundation models in a way compete with everyone. The second ingredient is the **lessons, understanding of users, and everything to which models have only limited access**. That could be built even while the technology was not yet ready. Between 2022 and 2024, Praktika was discovering what people want to use and how to reach the market, and that, Jacob says, cannot be extracted from a model.

Adam confirms this with an anecdote. The team recorded all early user conversations and still has hundreds of interviews from 2022. It is interesting, he says, that people in them say the exact same things as in today's interviews.
keywords_en: building on the frontier of technology

sections.subtitle: Hoće li univerzalni prevoditelj ubiti učenje jezika?
sections.screenshot_description: Adam Turaev prepričava priču američkog korisnika u Italiji koji je koristio avatara za razgovor s konobarima
sections.content:
Jacob pomalo izlazi iz plana razgovora i otvara pitanje vanjske prijetnje. Glasovni modeli ne služe samo za vježbanje jezika, nego mogu prevoditi i **u stvarnom vremenu**. Pita je li se raspoloženje prema učenju jezika promijenilo jer bi svi mogli dobiti nešto poput univerzalnog prevoditelja iz Zvjezdanih staza, ili je potražnja možda čak porasla.

Adam odgovara da to pitanje ne čuje od korisnika ni u razgovorima s njima, ali ga vrlo često čuje od **investitora**. Jacob se ironično šali da korisnici sigurno griješe, a ne „ljudi s novcem”. Adam priznaje da je o tome razmišljao i sam tim.

Zatim prepričava priču iz jednog intervjua. **Američki korisnik preselio se u Italiju** i zamolio Praktikina avatara da mu pomogne prevesti nešto konobarima. Umjesto Google Prevoditelja i njegovih glasova htio je da mu pomogne njegov coach u Praktici, koji mu tako nije bio samo učitelj, nego i vodič u stvarnom životu.

Jacob upozorava da je lako linearno ekstrapolirati ishode, a svijet je vrlo složen. Može čak zamisliti da će želja za učenjem jezika rasti jer bi umjetna inteligencija mogla povećati vrijednost susreta uživo. Kao netko tko je nekoliko jezika naučio, kaže da držanje aplikacije koja prevodi između osobe i konobara ne daje istu vrijednost. Takva je razmjena transakcijska i neugodno hladna. Razgovor na nečijem jeziku način je da se s tom osobom povežeš na ljudskoj razini, a to stroj ne može zamijeniti. Možda će takve vještine dobiti i dodatnu vrijednost: ako više ljudi bude htjelo putovati i družiti se uživo, učenje jezika moglo bi postati tržište u rastu.

Adam se slaže i objašnjava razliku. Jezik nije transakcijski i ljudi ga ne uče iz transakcijskih razloga. Za puke transakcije rješenja postoje već danas i ne treba čekati nove tehnologije. Tko želi **pripadati, integrirati se u novu kulturu i društvo**, mora govoriti jezik. Kao višejezični govornik dodaje da je čovjek u svakom jeziku pomalo drukčija osoba. Jacob se šali da je i on na drugom jeziku „Jacobo Loco”, mnogo druželjubiviji.
sections.subtitle_en: Will the Universal Translator Kill Language Learning?
sections.screenshot_description_en: Adam Turaev Recounts the Story of an American User in Italy Who Used the Avatar to Converse with Waiters
sections.content_en:
Jacob steps slightly outside the conversation plan and raises the question of an external threat. Voice models do not only serve for language practice, but can also translate **in real time**. He asks whether sentiment toward language learning has changed because everyone might get something like the universal translator from Star Trek, or whether demand has perhaps even increased.

Adam replies that he does not hear that question from users or in conversations with them, but he hears it very often from **investitors**. Jacob ironically jokes that users must be wrong, rather than the “people with money.” Adam admits that the team itself had thought about it as well.

Then he recounts a story from an interview. An **American user moved to Italy** and asked Praktika's avatar to help him translate something to waiters. Instead of Google Translate and its voices, he wanted his coach in Praktika to help him, who was thus not only a teacher to him, but also a guide in real life.

Jacob warns that it is easy to linearly extrapolate outcomes, yet the world is very complex. He can even imagine that the desire to learn languages will grow because artificial intelligence could increase the value of in-person encounters. As someone who has learned several languages, he says holding an app that translates between a person and a waiter does not provide the same value. Such an exchange is transactional and unpleasantly cold. Speaking in someone's language is a way to connect with that person on a human level, and a machine cannot replace that. Perhaps such skills will also gain additional value: if more people want to travel and socialize in person, language learning could become a growing market.

Adam agrees and explains the difference. Language is not transactional and people do not learn it for transactional reasons. For mere transactions, solutions exist even today and there is no need to wait for new technologies. Whoever wants **to belong, to integrate into a new culture and society**, must speak the language. As a multilingual speaker, he adds that a person is a slightly different person in each language. Jacob jokes that in another language he too is “Jacobo Loco,” much more outgoing.

sections.subtitle: Razgovor kao usko grlo: AI coach naspram općih modela
sections.screenshot_description: Adam Turaev objašnjava razliku između AI companiona i AI coacha te spominje CEFR razine
sections.content:
Jacob se prisjeća vremena prije RevenueCata, kada je jezike učio iz zabave uz servis s **ljudskim tutorima**. Danas mu je očito koliko je to bilo skupo. Za ozbiljno učenje s tutorom treba razgovarati otprilike jednom tjedno, a sat je stajao oko **50 dolara**, što je i u američkim dolarima mnogo. Pritom je potreban dobar tutor: izvorni govornik koji je ujedno i dobar učitelj.

Jacob ponavlja i svoje uvjerenje, uz ogradu da ne želi stalno kritizirati Duolingo, da je **razgovor ključno ograničenje** u učenju jezika. Razgovor opisuje kao prirodni, „unaprijed programirani” mehanizam kojim ljudski mozak usvaja jezik. Knjige i ostala pomagala izmišljene su naknadno, a ljudska neuronska mreža stvorena je da prima i proizvodi jezik. Iz iskustva učenika zaključuje da napredak raste s vremenom provedenim u slušanju i obradi jezika. Tek su nedavno, kaže, glasovni modeli postali dovoljno dobri za razgovor u stvarnom vremenu koji djeluje donekle uvjerljivo.

Adam tu povlači važnu granicu. S općim modelima, poput glasovnog načina rada u **ChatGPT-ju**, mogu se igrati uloge i dobiti partner za vježbu. Praktika ne nudi samo **AI companiona**, nego **AI coacha, odnosno AI tutora**. Jacob potvrđuje da je istog dana prošao uvodni postupak u aplikaciji i da je ona koristila **CEFR razine** (A1, B1, B2). Takve razine nikad nije vidio u nekom ležernom proizvodu za učenje jezika, nego samo kod pravih tutora koji ocjenjuju znanje.

Adam objašnjava da Praktika simulira **sigurno okruženje bez osuđivanja** u kojem se jezična barijera može probiti. Za mnoge korisnike to nije ni transakcija ni kulturna znatiželja. Jezik ih sprječava da dođu do sljedeće prekretnice, promaknuća ili prilike. Taj je proces bolan i zato treba netko tko pruža podršku u teškim trenucima. Usporedbu je jasna: netko može živjeti i bez učenja španjolskog i neće biti posljedica ako preskoči tjednu lekciju. Za korisnike Praktike to je možda jedina prilika da nauče jezik i dobiju šansu u životu.

Adam dodaje da su to shvatili rano jer su kao tri suosnivača isto proživjeli. Kada su probili jezičnu barijeru, otvorile su im se prilike više razine i, kako kaže, više nisu bili samo lokalni igrači.

Jacob zaključuje da je engleski globalni jezik kapitala i tehnologije. I tvrtke koje djeluju lokalno često rade na engleskom. U RevenueCatu je vjerojatno većini zaposlenih engleski drugi jezik, a ipak je zajednički. Budući da su vodeći AI laboratoriji američki i rade uglavnom na engleskom, iako se mnogo istraživanja odvija i u Kini, Jacob ne vidi da bi se trend preokrenuo. Engleski će, smatra, ostati zajednički jezik i u budućnosti.
sections.subtitle_en: Conversation as a Bottleneck: AI Coach Versus General Models
sections.screenshot_description_en: Adam Turaev Explains the Difference Between an AI Companion and an AI Coach and Mentions CEFR Levels
sections.content_en:
Jacob recalls the time before RevenueCat, when he learned languages for fun with a service featuring **human tutors**. Today it is obvious to him how expensive that was. For serious learning, one needs to speak with a tutor about once a week, and an hour cost around **50 dollars**, which is a lot even in US dollars. At the same time, a good tutor is needed: a native speaker who is also a good teacher.

Jacob also reiterates his conviction, with the caveat that he does not want to constantly criticize Duolingo, that **conversation is the key bottleneck** in language learning. He describes conversation as the natural, “pre-programmed” mechanism by which the human brain acquires language. Books and other aids were invented subsequently, and the human neural network was created to receive and produce language. From his experience as a learner, he concludes that progress increases with time spent listening to and processing language. Only recently, he says, have voice models become good enough for real-time conversation that feels somewhat convincing.

Adam draws an important line here. With general models, such as the voice mode in **ChatGPT**, one can role-play and get a practice partner. Praktika offers not just an **AI companion**, but an **AI coach, or an AI tutor**. Jacob confirms that on the same day he went through the onboarding process in the app and that it used **CEFR levels** (A1, B1, B2). He had never seen such levels in a casual language learning product, but only with real tutors who evaluate proficiency.

Adam explains that Praktika simulates a **safe environment without judgment** in which the language barrier can be broken. For many users, this is neither a transaction nor cultural curiosity. Language prevents them from reaching the next milestone, promotion, or opportunity. That process is painful, and that is why someone who provides support in difficult moments is needed. The comparison is clear: someone can live without learning Spanish, and there will be no consequences if they skip a weekly lesson. For Praktika users, this is perhaps their only opportunity to learn the language and get a chance in life.

Adam adds that they realized this early on because, as three co-founders, they experienced the same thing. When they broke through the language barrier, higher-level opportunities opened up for them and, as he says, they were no longer just local players.

Jacob concludes that English is the global language of capital and technology. Even companies that operate locally often work in English. At RevenueCat, English is probably a second language for the majority of employees, yet it is the common one. Since the leading AI labs are American and operate mostly in English, although a lot of research is also taking place in China, Jacob does not see the trend reversing. English will, he believes, remain the common language in the future as well.

sections.subtitle: Posao koji aplikacija obavlja za korisnika i ishodi kao prednost u eri umjetne inteligencije
sections.screenshot_description: David upozorava slušatelje da se vrate na prethodnih petnaestak minuta i razmisle o poslu koji aplikacija obavlja za korisnika
sections.content:
David najavljuje da će uskoro vratiti razgovor na rast aplikacije, a Jacob priznaje da je tržište učenja jezika jednostavno previše zanimljivo. Prije nastavka David se ipak obraća slušateljima. Neki će pomisliti da je sve dosad bilo specifično za učenje jezika, ali on preporučuje da se ponovno preslušaju posljednjih 10 do 15 minuta.

Sve što je Adam istaknuo, kaže David, vraća se na **posao koji aplikacija obavlja za korisnika** (*jobs to be done*). Cilj Praktike je da osoba koja ne govori engleski dobije bolji posao zato što ga je naučila. Kada se prodaje takav ishod, a ne učenje iz zabave kakvo prakticira Jacob, donose se potpuno drukčije odluke. To vrijedi za svaku aplikaciju: treba znati što se doista rješava za korisnika i ostati na tome usredotočen, čak i kada drugi smjerovi odvlače pažnju.

Adam smatra da je to osobito važno upravo u eri umjetne inteligencije, kada su svi nesigurni oko toga što je danas obrambena prednost tvrtke. Po njegovu mišljenju ona leži u **vlasništvu nad ishodima** i dosljednom fokusu na njih. Kada je cilj korisniku isporučiti ishod, prioritet dobivaju:
- kontekst,
- okvir oko modela (*harness*),
- korisničko iskustvo s jasnim stavovima.

To je, zaključuje Adam, ono što danas razlikuje proizvode: **ukus za proizvod**.

Jacob primjećuje da se o tome vodi velika rasprava: koliko prostora ostaje između modela i krajnjeg korisnika. Priznaje da mu je stav pomalo u vlastitom interesu, ali vjeruje da opće platforme poput ChatGPT-ja ili Claudea nikada neće moći obuhvatiti sve. Nema dovoljno površine i sve bi postalo previše složeno. Agent bi vjerojatno mogao složiti nešto osrednje kvalitete, ali specijalizirani tim uvijek može uzeti ono što agent može i nadograditi to: učiniti učinkovitijim, ciljanijim i jasnijim. Uz šaljivu ogradu, to vrijedi osim ako ne ide prema pravoj singularnosti.
keywords: posao koji aplikacija obavlja za korisnika
sections.subtitle_en: Jobs to Be Done by the App for the User and Outcomes as an Advantage in the AI Era
sections.screenshot_description_en: David Cautions Listeners to Go Back to the Previous Fifteen Minutes and Think About the Job the App Does for the User
sections.content_en:
David announces that he will soon bring the conversation back to app growth, and Jacob admits that the language learning market is simply too interesting. Before continuing, David nevertheless addresses the listeners. Some will think that everything so far was specific to language learning, but he recommends listening again to the last 10 to 15 minutes.

Everything Adam pointed out, David says, comes back to the **job the app does for the user** (*jobs to be done*). Praktika's goal is for a non-English speaker to get a better job because they learned it. When selling such an outcome, rather than learning for fun as Jacob practices, completely different decisions are made. This applies to every app: one needs to know what is truly being solved for the user and remain focused on that, even when other directions distract attention.

Adam believes this is especially important right now in the era of artificial intelligence, when everyone is unsure about what constitutes a company's defensible moat today. In his view, it lies in **ownership of outcomes** and consistent focus on them. When the goal is to deliver an outcome to the user, priority is given to:
- context,
- the framework around the model (*harness*),
- an opinionated user experience.

That is, Adam concludes, what differentiates products today: **product taste**.

Jacob remarks that a big debate is taking place over this: how much surface area remains between the model and the end user. He admits his stance is somewhat self-serving, but he believes that general platforms like ChatGPT or Claude will never be able to cover everything. There is not enough surface area and everything would become too complex. An agent could probably put together something of mediocre quality, but a specialized team can always take what the agent can do and build upon it: make it more effective, more targeted, and clearer. With a humorous caveat, that holds true unless we are heading toward a true singularity.
keywords_en: jobs to be done by the app for the user

sections.subtitle: Škole, regulacija i AI koji umnožava znanje tutora
sections.screenshot_description: Adam Turaev objašnjava kako bi tutori uz pomoć AI avatara mogli podučavati tisuću učenika umjesto dvadeset
sections.content:
Jacob otvara pitanje obrazovnog sustava. Praktikina tehnologija djelomično istiskuje postojeću infrastrukturu privatnih instrukcija. U zemljama u kojima engleski donosi ekonomsku korist njegovo je učenje u školama vjerojatno prioritet. Jacob iskreno priznaje da bi Praktika danas bila bolja od njegovih nekadašnjih profesora jezika. Šali se da bi bilo bolje zatvoriti učenike u prostoriju s aplikacijom nego im držati klasičnu nastavu stranog jezika. Pita kako Adam vidi obrazovni sustav kao dio svog ekosustava.

Adam kaže da bi Praktika voljela biti dio tog sustava, ali on prilično zaostaje zbog **regulacije**. Jacob dodaje da ni **sindikati učitelja** vjerojatno neće s oduševljenjem prihvatiti zamjenu avatarom.

Adam ipak naglašava da umjetna inteligencija neće potpuno zamijeniti tutore. Oni imaju jedinstveno znanje i metodologije, a njihova je misija sada, kaže, još važnija. Zalaže se za **partnerstvo**: zajedničku gradnju umjetne inteligencije koja može skalirati znanje i metode tutora. Jacob se slaže da bi svaki tutor rado s učenikom proveo 10 ili 20 sati tjedno, ali to si ne mogu priuštiti ni klijenti ni sami tutori, koji jednostavno nemaju dovoljno sati.

Adam objašnjava da tutori uz umjetnu inteligenciju, ako je koriste ispravno i ne boje je se, mogu umjesto **20 učenika podučavati 1000 ili više**, i to individualno, licem u lice. Prema njegovim riječima, već je moguće:
- klonirati vlastiti glas i lice,
- izgraditi vlastitog avatara,
- hraniti ga vlastitim kontekstom i posebnom pedagoškom formulom.

Takav avatar podučava učenike na način samog tutora. Adam naglašava da je upravo to jedinstveno i posebno jer ni najbolji modeli to ne mogu replicirati: svaki tutor ima vlastitu „DNK” svog rada.
sections.subtitle_en: Schools, Regulation, and AI That Multiplies Tutor Knowledge
sections.screenshot_description_en: Adam Turaev Explains How Tutors with the Help of AI Avatars Could Teach a Thousand Students Instead of Twenty
sections.content_en:
Jacob raises the question of the educational system. Praktika's technology partially displaces the existing infrastructure of private tutoring. In countries where English brings economic benefit, learning it in schools is probably a priority. Jacob honestly admits that Praktika today would be better than his former language teachers. He jokes that it would be better to lock students in a room with the app than to give them traditional foreign language classes. He asks how Adam sees the educational system as part of his ecosystem.

Adam says Praktika would love to be part of that system, but it lags behind considerably due to **regulation**. Jacob adds that **teachers' unions** will probably not enthusiastically embrace replacement by an avatar either.

Adam nevertheless emphasizes that artificial intelligence will not completely replace tutors. They have unique knowledge and methodologies, and their mission now, he says, is even more important. He advocates for a **partnership**: co-building artificial intelligence that can scale the knowledge and methods of tutors. Jacob agrees that every tutor would gladly spend 10 or 20 hours a week with a student, but neither clients nor tutors themselves, who simply do not have enough hours, can afford that.

Adam explains that tutors using artificial intelligence, if they use it properly and do not fear it, can teach **1,000 or more students instead of 20**, and do so individually, face-to-face. According to him, it is already possible to:
- clone one's own voice and face,
- build one's own avatar,
- feed it with one's own context and special pedagogical formula.

Such an avatar teaches students in the manner of the tutor himself. Adam emphasizes that this is precisely what is unique and special because even the best models cannot replicate it: every tutor has their own “DNA” of their work.

sections.subtitle: Zašto avatari u Pixar stilu: strah od govora, vježba stresa i neobična dolina
sections.screenshot_description: Adam Turaev objašnjava da su avatari nastali iz uvida da je strah glavni razlog zbog kojeg korisnici dolaze u aplikaciju
sections.content:
Jacob se vraća na plan razgovora i jednu od Praktikinih najprepoznatljivijih odluka: avatare u stilu Pixara, barem kada je riječ o novijima. Iz vlastitog iskustva kaže da isprva djeluju pomalo jezivo, ali su vizualno vrlo razumljivi i olakšavaju sadržajni marketing jer se vidi kako lik govori. Smatra da se avatari uživo tek izvlače iz **neobične doline** (*uncanny valley*) i da je tek ove godine vidio prve koji nisu neugodni. Adam misli da ta neugodnost još djelomično postoji, a Jacob se slaže da još nisu na cilju, ali da nisu daleko. Pita zašto je tim toliko uložio u avatare i stavio ih u središte iskustva.

Adam priznaje da bi odgovor mogao biti kontroverzan: odluka **nikad nije bila motivirana marketingom ni distribucijom**. Polazište je bilo razumijevanje da jezična barijera nije samo pitanje vještine. Velik dio problema je **psihološki**: razgovor s drugim čovjekom na stranom jeziku traži brzo razmišljanje i izrazito je stresan.

Ključni uvid stigao je iz uvodnog postupka u aplikaciji. Jedan od glavnih razloga zbog kojih ljudi dolaze bio je **strah**, a među najčešće odabranim odgovorima bili su upravo strah i želja za uvježbavanjem razgovora. Zato su avatari napravljeni tako da simuliraju razgovor s drugom osobom.

Tehnologija pritom nije morala savršeno oponašati čovjeka. Dovoljan je osjećaj da te netko gleda. Taj osjećaj stvara simulirano stresno okruženje u kojem korisnik uvježbava upravo tu nelagodu. Zato je korisnicima Praktike kasnije mnogo lakše govoriti jezik sa stvarnim ljudima. Adam se prisjeća da je to bio jedan od najpropitkivanijih dijelova proizvoda kada su prikupljali prvi krug ulaganja, a danas je, kaže, očito zašto je potreban.

Jacob predviđa da će za godinu do tri izrada avatara biti jeftinija, a kvaliteta viša. Priznaje da i sam još koluta očima na neke nove avatare koje vidi, ali se sam podsjeća da će za 12 mjeseci vjerojatno biti tamo gdje trebaju biti. Adam se slaže i naglašava da tim nije „religiozno” vezan uz Pixar estetiku. Zasad je to jednostavno najbolji način da se korisnicima pruži takvo iskustvo, a da ih se ne prestraši.

Jacob objašnjava logiku: avatar koji pokušava biti previše ljudski upada duboko u neobičnu dolinu, dok crtani stil to olakšava. Zato, primjećuje, i AI generirane dramske serije često koriste crtani, pixarovski stil. Adam dodaje da ni **Muse, Dots** i drugi ne lansiraju ljudske avatare. Jacob zaključuje da su prije tridesetak godina postojali vrlo neugodni pokušaji ljudskih avatara i da su ljudi od toga još uvijek pomalo opečeni.
sections.subtitle_en: Why Pixar-Style Avatars: Fear of Speaking, Stress Practice, and the Uncanny Valley
sections.screenshot_description_en: Adam Turaev Explains That the Avatars Were Born from the Insight That Fear Is the Main Reason Users Come to the App
sections.content_en:
Jacob returns to the conversation plan and one of Praktika's most recognizable decisions: Pixar-style avatars, at least when it comes to newer ones. From his own experience, he says that at first they seem a bit creepy, but they are visually very understandable and facilitate content marketing because one sees how the character speaks. He believes that live avatars are only just pulling out of the **uncanny valley** and that only this year did he see the first ones that are not uncomfortable. Adam thinks that discomfort still partially exists, and Jacob agrees that they are not at the goal yet, but they are not far off. He asks why the team invested so much in avatars and placed them at the center of the experience.

Adam admits that the answer could be controversial: the decision **was never motivated by marketing or distribution**. The starting point was the understanding that the language barrier is not just a matter of skill. A large part of the problem is **psychological**: speaking with another human in a foreign language requires quick thinking and is extremely stressful.

The key insight came from the onboarding process in the app. One of the main reasons people came was **fear**, and among the most frequently selected answers were precisely fear and the desire to practice conversation. That is why the avatars were made to simulate a conversation with another person.

The technology, moreover, did not have to mimic a human perfectly. The feeling that someone is looking at you is enough. That feeling creates a simulated stressful environment in which the user practices that exact discomfort. That is why it is later much easier for Praktika users to speak the language with real people. Adam recalls that this was one of the most questioned parts of the product when they were raising their first funding round, and today, he says, it is obvious why it is needed.

Jacob predicts that in one to three years avatar creation will be cheaper and quality higher. He admits that he still rolls his eyes at some new avatars he sees, but he reminds himself that in 12 months they will probably be where they need to be. Adam agrees and emphasizes that the team is not “religiously” attached to the Pixar aesthetic. For now, it is simply the best way to provide users with such an experience without scaring them.

Jacob explains the logic: an avatar trying to be too human falls deep into the uncanny valley, whereas a cartoon style makes it easier. That is why, he notes, AI-generated drama series often use a cartoon, Pixar-like style as well. Adam adds that neither **Muse, Dots**, nor others launch human avatars. Jacob concludes that thirty-odd years ago there were very uncomfortable attempts at human avatars and that people are still somewhat burned by that.
