sections.subtitle: Mali profili, velik doseg: kako je Praktika krenula u lov na mikroinfluencere
sections.screenshot_description: Adam Turaev objašnjava kako je na platformi Modash filtrirao influencere s malo pratitelja, a velikim dosegom
sections.content:
Nakon rasprave o avatarima voditelj **David** prelazi na rast, temu koja, kako kaže, najviše zanima slušatelje. Zanima ga koliko su mikroinfluenceri pridonijeli brzom skaliranju Praktike i kako je ta priča počela.

**Adam Turaev** odmah ispravlja pretpostavku da je postojala unaprijed smišljena strategija mikroinfluencera. Polazište je bilo jednostavno i pomalo prisilno: tvrtka nije imala budžet za velike influencere u regiji, pa je trebalo pronaći nekoga tko je tek u usponu. Pomogla mu je platforma **Modash**, koja je i sama tada bila u ranoj fazi. Ona je omogućila filtriranje po broju pratitelja, a to je u to vrijeme bio glavni pokazatelj cijene: tko ima velik broj pratitelja, naplaćuje skupo.

Adam je zato postavio granicu od **manje od 5.000 pratitelja**, a zatim izdvojio profile koji unatoč tome skupljaju velik broj pregleda, odnosno one koje algoritam trenutačno gura. Tako je pronašao kreatora čiji su edukativni videi tada dosezali desetke milijuna pregleda. Taj kreator nije imao ni e-mail adresu za suradnju, a Adam ističe da nije ni bio svjestan koliko je zapravo uspješan. Adam mu se zato javio izravnim porukom na TikToku i predložio suradnju jer se činilo da se dobro uklapaju.

Riječ je o **Gustavu**, koji je danas zaposlenik Praktike. Adam ga opisuje kao „iznimno talentiranog“. Gustavo i dalje snima videe za tvrtku, vodi njezine društvene mreže i neko je vrijeme bio svojevrsno lice Praktike.

**Jacob** sažima logiku pristupa. Malo pratitelja i velik doseg dobar su pokazatelj da je riječ o nekome u usponu: publiku još nije stekao, ali algoritam je već prepoznao njegov sadržaj. Prema Jacobu, preglede tada pokreće sam sadržaj, a ne postojeća baza pratitelja, što je vrijednije kada se procjenjuje cijena takve suradnje. Zato ga uspoređuje s potragom za podcijenjenom imovinom.

Adam tu usporedbu dodatno precizira. Ne radi se toliko o tome da je netko podcijenjen, nego o tome da mu se pristupa **prije nego što dosegne vrhunac**. Jacob se slaže i dodaje da nije mislio kako takvim kreatorima nužno treba manje platiti. Riječ je o ulasku u pravom trenutku, kao kod kupnje dionica, kada svi na kraju profitiraju. Adam vjeruje da taj okvir i danas funkcionira: ne treba ciljati isključivo mikroinfluencere, nego tražiti one koji s malim brojem pratitelja ostvaruju velik broj pregleda.
sections.subtitle_en: Small Profiles, Huge Reach: How Praktika Began Hunting for Micro-Influencers
sections.screenshot_description_en: Adam Turaev Explains How on the Modash Platform He Filtered Influencers with Few Followers and Large Reach
sections.content_en:
After the discussion about avatars, host **David** turns to growth, the topic that, as he says, interests listeners the most. He is curious how much micro-influencers contributed to Praktika's rapid scaling and how that story began.

**Adam Turaev** immediately corrects the assumption that there was a pre-planned micro-influencer strategy. The starting point was simple and somewhat forced: the company did not have a budget for large influencers in the region, so they had to find someone who was just on the rise. He was helped by the **Modash** platform, which was itself in an early stage at the time. It enabled filtering by follower count, and that was the main price indicator back then: whoever has a large number of followers charges a high price.

Adam therefore set a limit of **fewer than 5,000 followers**, and then singled out profiles that nevertheless racked up a large number of views, that is, those that the algorithm was currently boosting. That is how he found a creator whose educational videos were reaching tens of millions of views at the time. That creator did not even have an email address for collaborations, and Adam points out that he was not even aware of how successful he actually was. Adam therefore reached out to him via direct message on TikTok and proposed a collaboration because it seemed they were a good fit.

That person is **Gustavo**, who is today a Praktika employee. Adam describes him as “extremely talented.” Gustavo still shoots videos for the company, manages its social media, and was for a time the sort of face of Praktika.

**Jacob** summarizes the logic of the approach. Few followers and a large reach are a good indicator that it is someone on the rise: they have not yet built an audience, but the algorithm has already recognized their content. According to Jacob, views are then driven by the content itself rather than an existing follower base, which is more valuable when evaluating the price of such a collaboration. That is why he compares it to searching for undervalued assets.

Adam further refines that comparison. It is not so much that someone is undervalued, but that they are approached **before reaching their peak**. Jacob agrees and adds that he did not mean that such creators should necessarily be paid less. It is about entering at the right moment, as with buying stocks, when everyone ultimately profits. Adam believes that framework still works today: one should not target micro-influencers exclusively, but look for those who achieve a large number of views with a small number of followers.

sections.subtitle: Deset mjeseci poruka i jedan video od 30 milijuna pregleda
sections.screenshot_description: Adam Turaev prepričava kako je Gustavov video, koji mu se isprva nije svidio, postao viralan na tri platforme
sections.content:
Na Jacobovo pitanje je li kontaktirao velik broj ljudi pa dobio tek nekoliko pogodaka, Adam odgovara potvrdno. Imao je dugačak popis kreatora, a tada nije bilo današnjih alata za automatizaciju. Kao osnivač je, procjenjuje, oko **deset mjeseci** puno radno vrijeme slao e-mailove i poruke influencerima. Uspjelo je tek s nekolicinom njih.

Gustava posebno spominje zbog jednog videa. Gustavo mu je poslao snimku, a Adamova reakcija bila je mlaka. Prema vlastitim riječima, rekao mu je da mu se video ne sviđa, ali da ga slobodno objavi. Video je potom eksplodirao:

- **oko 10 milijuna pregleda na Instagramu**,
- **još oko 10 milijuna na TikToku**,
- **još oko 10 milijuna na YouTubeu**.

Adam kaže da je to bio trenutak u kojem je Praktika vrlo brzo narasla s otprilike **1 milijuna dolara godišnjeg ponavljajućeg prihoda (ARR) na 10 do 12 milijuna**.

David se nadovezuje s nevjericom: u pitanju je skok s jednog na dvanaest milijuna ARR-a u samo mjesec dana. Zanima ga je li za to zaslužan samo Gustavov video ili je tvrtka isti format počela ponavljati iznova.
sections.subtitle_en: Ten Months of Messages and One Video with 30 Million Views
sections.screenshot_description_en: Adam Turaev Recounts How Gustavo's Video, Which He Did Not Like at First, Went Viral on Three Platforms
sections.content_en:
To Jacob's question of whether he contacted a large number of people only to get a few hits, Adam answers affirmatively. He had a long list of creators, and the automation tools of today did not exist back then. As a founder, he estimates, he spent about **ten months** full-time sending emails and direct messages to influencers. It succeeded with only a handful of them.

He mentions Gustavo specifically because of one video. Gustavo sent him a clip, and Adam's reaction was lukewarm. In his own words, he told him he did not like the video, but that he was free to post it. The video then exploded:

- **about 10 million views on Instagram**,
- **another roughly 10 million on TikTok**,
- **another roughly 10 million on YouTube**.

Adam says that was the moment when Praktika very quickly grew from approximately **1 million dollars in annual recurring revenue (ARR) to 10 to 12 million**.

David follows up in disbelief: it is a jump from one to twelve million ARR in just one month. He wonders whether Gustavo's video alone was responsible for that or if the company began repeating the same format over and over.

sections.subtitle: Coach koji ispravlja pogreške: format koji su kopirale sve aplikacije za učenje jezika
sections.screenshot_description: Adam Turaev opisuje strukturu viralnog videa u kojem AI coach ispravlja korisnikove pogreške
sections.content:
Adam objašnjava da je struktura tog videa danas **osnovni format videa za aplikacije za učenje jezika**. Gustavo je Brazilac, pa je, prema Adamu, iz prve ruke poznavao bolnu točku svoje publike. Zato je osmislio video s kratkim razgovorom u kojem coach jednostavno ispravlja pogreške.

Jacob odmah prepoznaje format: netko nešto kaže, a coach ga ispravi. Priznaje da ga takvi videi privlače iako nije siguran zašto. Adam otkriva da je i sam bio skeptičan. Pitao je Gustava zašto ne govori o aplikaciji i ne pokaže je, a Gustavo mu je odgovorio da mu jednostavno vjeruje. Adam je pristao.

Jacob nudi i psihološko objašnjenje. Smatra da ljudi imaju snažan poriv da isprave nekoga tko griješi. Za usporedbu navodi poznati meme video u kojem netko stavlja oblike u pogrešne otvore, zbog čega gledatelji „viču na ekran“. Pretpostavlja da takvi videi ne ciljaju potpune početnike, nego ljude koji su već prošli nekoliko lekcija. Oni pogrešku prepoznaju i osjećaju zadovoljstvo što su je uočili.

Jacob rast uspoređuje s istraživanjem velikog prostora mogućnosti. Postoji mnogo varijabli, a netko slučajno isproba nešto što pogodi novi globalni optimum. Dodaje da konkurenti sada vjerojatno koriste isti format, ali je Praktika iskoristila prednost dok je to bilo moguće.
sections.subtitle_en: A Coach Correcting Mistakes: The Format Copied by All Language Learning Apps
sections.screenshot_description_en: Adam Turaev Describes the Structure of the Viral Video in Which an AI Coach Corrects the User's Mistakes
sections.content_en:
Adam explains that the structure of that video is today the **fundamental video format for language learning apps**. Gustavo is Brazilian, so, according to Adam, he knew the pain point of his audience firsthand. That is why he devised a video with a short conversation in which the coach simply corrects mistakes.

Jacob immediately recognizes the format: someone says something, and the coach corrects them. He admits that such videos attract him even though he is not sure why. Adam reveals that he was skeptical himself. He asked Gustavo why he did not talk about the app and show it, and Gustavo answered to simply trust him. Adam agreed.

Jacob also offers a psychological explanation. He believes people have a strong urge to correct someone making a mistake. For comparison, he cites the well-known meme video in which someone puts shapes into the wrong slots, causing viewers to “yell at the screen.” He assumes that such videos do not target complete beginners, but people who have already completed several lessons. They recognize the mistake and feel satisfaction at noticing it.

Jacob compares growth to exploring a large space of possibilities. There are many variables, and someone accidentally tries something that hits a new global optimum. He adds that competitors are now probably using the same format, but Praktika capitalized on the advantage while it was possible.

sections.subtitle: Repliciranje formata diljem svijeta uz gotovo nulti trošak
sections.screenshot_description: Adam Turaev objašnjava kako su viralni format počeli replicirati s kreatorima u drugim zemljama
sections.content:
David se vraća na mehaniku rasta. Gustavov video skupio je oko 30 milijuna pregleda na tri platforme, ali sumnja da je on sam mogao podići prihod s jednog na dvanaest milijuna u mjesec dana. Pita koliko je kreatora uspjelo ponoviti uspjeh i kako je bilo unutar tvrtke tijekom tog mjeseca.

Adam priznaje da tim isprva nije ni shvaćao što se događa. Vidjeli su samo da nešto radi i odlučili to skalirati što brže mogu. Počeli su replicirati videe **s kreatorima u drugim zemljama** kako bi ubrzali taj proces.

Jacob primjećuje da to zvuči kao dugotrajan posao jer postoji mnogo kombinacija izvornih i ciljnih jezika, avatara i ljudi. Adam odgovara da mnogi današnji lansirani proizvodi upravo zato ciljaju samo određene zemlje. U ovom je slučaju, međutim, tim vidio priliku da format relativno brzo skalira globalno, pa su ga počeli ponavljati iz različitih kutova.

Na Davidovo pitanje jesu li iza toga stajala i plaćena oglašavanja, Adam kaže da su uložili tek **malen budžet**. U prvim danima, prema njegovim riječima, bili su „ludi“ rezultati: troškovi po tisuću prikaza (CPM), po instalaciji (CPI), po probnom razdoblju i po kupnji bili su **gotovo nula**.
sections.subtitle_en: Replicating the Format Worldwide at Virtually Zero Cost
sections.screenshot_description_en: Adam Turaev Explains How They Began Replicating the Viral Format with Creators in Other Countries
sections.content_en:
David returns to the mechanics of growth. Gustavo's video racked up around 30 million views across three platforms, but he doubts that it alone could have raised revenue from one to twelve million in a month. He asks how many creators managed to repeat the success and what it was like inside the company during that month.

Adam admits that at first the team did not even realize what was happening. They only saw that something was working and decided to scale it as quickly as they could. They started replicating the videos **with creators in other countries** to accelerate that process.

Jacob remarks that this sounds like time-consuming work because there are many combinations of native and target languages, avatars, and people. Adam replies that many products launched today target only specific countries precisely because of that. In this case, however, the team saw an opportunity to scale the format globally relatively quickly, so they began repeating it from different angles.

To David's question of whether paid ads were behind this as well, Adam says they invested only a **small budget**. In the early days, according to his words, the results were “crazy”: costs per thousand impressions (CPM), per install (CPI), per trial, and per purchase were **virtually zero**.

sections.subtitle: „Odmah sam ga zaposlio“: pravilo da se influencerima ne govori kako da rade svoj posao
sections.screenshot_description: Adam Turaev iznosi svoje pravilo da influencerima ne treba govoriti kako da rade svoj posao
sections.content:
David pita kakav je bio aranžman s Gustavom. Mnogi današnji ugovori s influencerima predviđaju bonuse za određeni broj pregleda, pa ga zanima je li Gustavo dobro zaradio ili je već tada bio zaposlenik. Adam kratko odgovara: **zaposlio ga je odmah**, jer mu je takav čovjek trebao.

Jacob se šali da mu je „stavio prsten na prst“. Posebno mu se sviđa to što se Adamu video isprva nije svidio. Priznaje da se slične situacije često događaju i u RevenueCatu: neke stvari koje bi on ugasio pokazale su se dobrima, a neke koje nije ugasio poželio je da jest. David ga zadirkuje da mora pogoditi koje su koje.

Jacob iz toga izvlači širu pouku. Da bi se otkrilo što funkcionira, treba istražiti velik prostor mogućnosti. Ako se ugasi sve što se logički ne čini obećavajućim, takve prilike propadnu. Postoji ravnoteža između rizika koje brend smije preuzeti i pretjeranog uređivanja, a stvari se danas odvijaju toliko brzo da se mnogo toga može isprobati. Kada neka luda ideja marketinškog tima ne uspije, RevenueCat se jednostavno pravi da se nije dogodila. David pita misli li pritom na Ricka. Jacob diplomatski odgovara da neki pojedinci proizvode stvari „izvan distribucije“ više od drugih. Kao lekciju koju je naučio prekasno ističe da će osnivač koji sve propušta kroz vlastiti filter odobravanja propustiti ono što mu je u slijepoj točki.

Adam potvrđuje da mu je to pravilo od početka: **influencerima se ne govori kako da rade svoj posao**. Kad Jacob primijeti da bi osnivač, kada bi bio toliko utjecajan, videe snimao sam, Adam se slaže. Influenceri se angažiraju upravo zato što postižu izniman doseg, pa ih treba pustiti da rade svoj posao.
sections.subtitle_en: “I Hired Him Immediately”: The Rule of Not Telling Influencers How to Do Their Job
sections.screenshot_description_en: Adam Turaev Presents His Rule That One Should Not Tell Influencers How to Do Their Job
sections.content_en:
David asks what the arrangement with Gustavo was like. Many modern contracts with influencers provide bonuses for a certain number of views, so he wonders whether Gustavo earned well or was already an employee back then. Adam answers briefly: **he hired him immediately**, because he needed such a person.

Jacob jokes that he “put a ring on his finger.” He particularly likes the fact that Adam did not like the video at first. He admits that similar situations often happen at RevenueCat: some things he would have shut down turned out to be good, and some that he did not shut down he wished he had. David teases him that he has to guess which are which.

Jacob draws a broader lesson from this. To discover what works, one must explore a large space of possibilities. If everything that does not logically seem promising is shut down, such opportunities are lost. There is a balance between the risks a brand may take and excessive editing, and things move so fast today that a lot can be tried. When some crazy idea from the marketing team fails, RevenueCat simply pretends it never happened. David asks whether he means Rick by that. Jacob diplomatically replies that some individuals produce things “outside the distribution” more than others. As a lesson he learned too late, he points out that a founder who filters everything through their own approval filter will miss what is in their blind spot.

Adam confirms that this has been his rule from the beginning: **you don't tell influencers how to do their job**. When Jacob notes that if a founder were that influential, they would shoot the videos themselves, Adam agrees. Influencers are hired precisely because they achieve extraordinary reach, so they should be allowed to do their job.

sections.subtitle: Program kreatora danas: bivša influencerica na čelu i više od 100 suradnika
sections.screenshot_description: Adam Turaev opisuje strukturu programa kreatora s voditeljicom i coachevima po zemljama
sections.content:
Na Davidovo pitanje kako program influencera izgleda danas, Adam kaže da je pristup ostao isti. Uvijek mu je draže kada ljude ima unutar tvrtke. Praktika danas ima **program kreatora** s voditeljicom programa i coachevima influencera zaduženima za pojedine zemlje.

Adam o tome ima jasno mišljenje. Na tim pozicijama nalaze se **bivši influenceri** koji su nekada snimali videe za Praktiku jer znaju prepoznati dobar sadržaj, a to smatra ključnom vještinom. Upravljački dio posla, kaže, može se riješiti, pogotovo danas, i nije osobito kompliciran. Voditeljica programa je kreatorica iz **Poljske** koja je snimala videe za tvrtku. Bila je toliko uspješna da su je zaposlili, a sada vodi cijeli program.

Struktura izgleda ovako:

- **voditeljica programa** nadzire cjelinu,
- **coachevi influencera** vode pojedine zemlje,
- svaki coach ima **20 do 30 influencera** koji rotiraju različite pristupe sadržaju.

Na Jacobovo pitanje Adam pojašnjava da su voditelji i coachevi zaposlenici, a influenceri vanjski suradnici. Jacob to povezuje s načelom da umjetnike treba pustiti da budu umjetnici, bez odnosa šefa i zaposlenika. Adam ipak dodaje da stalno traži talente koje bi mogao dovesti u tvrtku.

Gustavo je zaseban slučaj: radi kao **interni influencer**. Program kreatora trenutačno broji **više od 100 influencera** i nastavlja rasti uz stalnu rotaciju jer, prema Adamu, u različitim zemljama ima još mnogo prilika.

Na Jacobovo pitanje o alatima Adam kaže da program vode putem platforme **SiteShift**, koju, kako tvrdi, danas koriste gotovo svi. Tim je na nju dogradio nekoliko vlastitih internih dodataka za detaljniju analitiku i izvještavanje. Jacob primjećuje da je kod ovakvih dvostranih tržišta uvijek korisno imati centralizirani alat.
sections.subtitle_en: The Creator Program Today: A Former Influencer at the Helm and Over 100 Collaborators
sections.screenshot_description_en: Adam Turaev Describes the Structure of the Creator Program with a Lead and Coaches by Country
sections.content_en:
To David's question of what the influencer program looks like today, Adam says the approach has remained the same. He always prefers having people in-house. Praktika today has a **creator program** with a program lead and influencer coaches responsible for individual countries.

Adam has a clear opinion on this. Those positions are held by **former influencers** who used to shoot videos for Praktika because they know how to recognize good content, which he considers a key skill. The management part of the job, he says, can be solved, especially today, and is not particularly complicated. The program lead is a creator from **Poland** who used to make videos for the company. She was so successful that they hired her, and now she runs the entire program.

The structure looks like this:

- the **program lead** oversees the whole,
- **influencer coaches** manage individual countries,
- each coach has **20 to 30 influencers** who rotate different content approaches.

To Jacob's question, Adam clarifies that the leads and coaches are employees, while the influencers are external collaborators. Jacob connects this with the principle that artists should be allowed to be artists, without a boss-employee relationship. Adam nevertheless adds that he is constantly looking for talent he can bring into the company.

Gustavo is a separate case: he works as an **internal influencer**. The creator program currently counts **over 100 influencers** and continues to grow with constant rotation because, according to Adam, there are still many opportunities in different countries.

To Jacob's question about tools, Adam says they run the program through the **SiteShift** platform, which, as he claims, almost everyone uses today. The team built several of their own internal add-ons on top of it for more detailed analytics and reporting. Jacob remarks that with such two-sided markets, it is always useful to have a centralized tool.

sections.subtitle: Fiksni iznos i bonus po pregledima, ali talent ima prednost
sections.screenshot_description: Adam Turaev objašnjava fleksibilnu strukturu ugovora s influencerima
sections.content:
David primjećuje da svaki sugovornik ima drukčiju filozofiju sklapanja ugovora s influencerima. Neki plaćaju po pregledu, neki fiksni iznos po videu uz bonuse, a neki rade po affiliate modelu. Zanima ga kako to radi Praktika.

Adam objašnjava da im struktura s coachevima influencera omogućuje fleksibilnost. Optimiziraju se za **najbolji talent**, a to ponekad zahtijeva i posebne uvjete ugovora. Nema krutog pravila po kojem se nudi isključivo fiksni iznos uz bonus. Ako je riječ o dobrom talentu, tim učini što god treba da ga angažira.

Tipičan aranžman ipak nije ništa posebno: sastoji se od **fiksnog dijela** i **bonusa ovisnog o broju pregleda**.
sections.subtitle_en: Fixed Fee and Bonus per Views, but Talent Takes Priority
sections.screenshot_description_en: Adam Turaev Explains the Flexible Structure of Contracts with Influencers
sections.content_en:
David remarks that every guest has a different philosophy of contracting with influencers. Some pay per view, some a fixed amount per video with bonuses, and some work on an affiliate model. He wonders how Praktika does it.

Adam explains that their structure with influencer coaches allows them flexibility. They optimize for the **best talent**, and that sometimes requires special contract terms as well. There is no rigid rule under which only a fixed amount with a bonus is offered. If it is a good talent, the team does whatever it takes to hire them.

A typical arrangement is nevertheless nothing special: it consists of a **fixed part** and a **bonus dependent on the number of views**.

sections.subtitle: Organski sadržaj i plaćeni oglasi: dva odvojena toka
sections.screenshot_description: Adam Turaev objašnjava zašto Praktika ne miješa program kreatora s plaćenom akvizicijom
sections.content:
David pita koliko viralnih videa završi kao oglasi i kako Praktika usklađuje plaćeno i organsko oglašavanje. U pitanje mu se pritom potkrao jezični lapsus, a Jacob dobacuje urednicima da to ostave u snimci.

Adam objašnjava da su plaćeni oglasi i organski sadržaj iz programa kreatora **dva odvojena toka**. Ne miješaju ih jer žele ostati vjerni načelu da influenceri sami smišljaju ideje i pristupe. Prema njegovim riječima, unutar tvrtke u nekom trenutku nastupi **zamor**: postaje teško smisliti nove pristupe i ponude. Svaki novi influencer zato donosi potencijal za nov način razmišljanja.

Veza među tokovima ipak postoji. Kada neki video postane viralan, dijeli se s timom za plaćenu akviziciju. Taj tim ga zatim reproducira sa svojim skupom internih influencera, vanjskih suradnika i kreatora sadržaja.
sections.subtitle_en: Organic Content and Paid Ads: Two Separate Streams
sections.screenshot_description_en: Adam Turaev Explains Why Praktika Does Not Mix the Creator Program with Paid Acquisition
sections.content_en:
David asks how many viral videos end up as ads and how Praktika balances paid and organic advertising. A slip of the tongue crept into his question, and Jacob tells the editors to leave it in the recording.

Adam explains that paid ads and organic content from the creator program are **two separate streams**. They do not mix them because they want to stay true to the principle that influencers come up with ideas and approaches on their own. According to his words, at some point **fatigue** sets in within the company: it becomes difficult to come up with new angles and offers. Every new influencer therefore brings potential for a new way of thinking.

A link between the streams nevertheless exists. When a video goes viral, it is shared with the paid acquisition team. That team then reproduces it with its own set of internal influencers, external collaborators, and content creators.

sections.subtitle: Avatari koji psuju: kad viralni marketing uđe u proizvod
sections.screenshot_description: Adam Turaev objašnjava zašto su 'unhinged' avatari unutar aplikacije bili promašaj
sections.content:
Prije nego što zaključi temu viralnog sadržaja, David spominje nekoliko promašaja s „unhinged“ oglasima. Jacob se prisjeća da je ranije u razgovoru predložio upravo takve avatare, a Adam je tada utihnuo.

Adam objašnjava što se dogodilo. U jednom su trenutku ludi, neobuzdani avatari postajali viralni na vrhu prodajnog lijevka. Zatim se nametnula logična ideja da ih se uvede i u aplikaciju. To, međutim, nije uspjelo. Mnogi korisnici bili su nezadovoljni i nisu razumjeli zašto njihov avatar psuje. Izgled im je bio u redu i htjeli su razgovarati s avatarom, ali psovanje ih je smetalo. Tim je zato odlučio da u Praktici neće biti avatara koji psuju.

Adam to povezuje s temeljnim načelom tvrtke: Praktika ne nudi **AI pratitelje**, nego **AI coacheve**, a od coacha se očekuje da bude nešto ozbiljniji.

Jacob dodaje da mnogi korisnici jednostavno ne razumiju šalu jer nisu na TikToku. Kao primjer navodi Duolingovu sovu Duo, koja je na društvenim mrežama mnogo luđa nego u samoj aplikaciji. Slično iskustvo ima i RevenueCat sa svojim čudnim mačkama: ideje se nižu, a onda nešto prijeđe nevidljivu granicu i treba se povući. Jacob priznaje da ponekad mora biti „kvaritelj zabave“ jer ono što je neobično i zabavno donosi viralnost, ali ima i cijenu ako se ne drži u pravom kontekstu. Zato je, kaže, humor težak: ista šala može potpuno drukčije odjeknuti ovisno o kontekstu.
sections.subtitle_en: Cursing Avatars: When Viral Marketing Enters the Product
sections.screenshot_description_en: Adam Turaev Explains Why 'Unhinged' Avatars Inside the App Were a Failure
sections.content_en:
Before concluding the topic of viral content, David mentions several failures with “unhinged” ads. Jacob recalls that earlier in the conversation he suggested precisely such avatars, and Adam went silent at that point.

Adam explains what happened. At one point, crazy, unhinged avatars were going viral at the top of the funnel. Then the logical idea arose to introduce them into the app as well. That, however, did not work. Many users were dissatisfied and did not understand why their avatar was cursing. The appearance was fine to them and they wanted to converse with the avatar, but the cursing bothered them. The team therefore decided that there would be no cursing avatars in Praktika.

Adam connects this with the fundamental principle of the company: Praktika does not offer **AI companions**, but **AI coaches**, and a coach is expected to be somewhat more serious.

Jacob adds that many users simply do not get the joke because they are not on TikTok. As an example, he cites Duolingo's owl Duo, which is much crazier on social media than in the app itself. RevenueCat has a similar experience with its weird cats: ideas keep coming, and then something crosses an invisible line and has to be walked back. Jacob admits that sometimes he has to be the “buzzkill” because what is unusual and funny brings virality, but it also has a cost if it is not kept in the right context. That is why, he says, humor is difficult: the same joke can resonate completely differently depending on the context.

sections.subtitle: Jedna stranica pravila za proizvod, sloboda za rast
sections.screenshot_description: Adam Turaev objašnjava razliku između slobode u marketingu i jasnih granica unutar proizvoda
sections.content:
Adam zaključuje da je sasvim u redu povući jasnu granicu: proizvod ima svoja zaštitna pravila (*guardrails*), a rast smije imati više slobode. Jacob se slaže i povlači paralelu s RevenueCatom. Ono što se objavi na Twitteru prolazno je i nestane, ali ono što je trajno drugačija je priča.

Kao ilustraciju navodi maskote **RC friends**, male likove koje jako voli. U nekom su trenutku, bez formalne odluke, završili na svakoj stranici nadzorne ploče. Jednog se jutra Jacob probudio i učinilo mu se da proizvod izgleda kao McDonald'sov restoran, s likovima posvuda. Zaključio je da ih treba ograničiti jer im je mjesto samo kao blagom začinu. Primjećuje i da Adam koristi izraz *guardrails*, kakav se inače daje AI agentu, te smatra da je to točan pojam: netko mora definirati granice za svako područje.

David pita kako Praktika tu ravnotežu postiže u praksi. Smiju li društvene mreže i rast biti potpuno neobuzdani, ili i tamo postoji gornja granica, samo viša nego u proizvodu?

Adam odgovara da su granice za proizvod **vrlo jasne**. Tim se interno dogovorio što radi, a što ne, a sve to stane na **jednu stranicu opisa** jer ne mora biti komplicirano. U području rasta influencere se pušta da rade svoj posao. Postoje neka osnovna ograničenja, ali je razlika prema Adamovim riječima vrlo velika. Vjerni svom načelu, influencerima dopuštaju da smisle gotovo bilo koji pristup koji žele.
sections.subtitle_en: A One-Page Rulebook for the Product, Freedom for Growth
sections.screenshot_description_en: Adam Turaev Explains the Difference Between Freedom in Marketing and Clear Guardrails Inside the Product
sections.content_en:
Adam concludes that it is entirely fine to draw a clear line: the product has its guardrails (*guardrails*), and growth is allowed more freedom. Jacob agrees and draws a parallel with RevenueCat. What is posted on Twitter is ephemeral and goes away, but what is permanent is a different story.

As an illustration, he mentions the **RC friends** mascots, little characters he likes a lot. At one point, without a formal decision, they ended up on every page of the dashboard. One morning Jacob woke up and felt that the product looked like a McDonald's restaurant, with characters everywhere. He concluded that they should be limited because their place is only as a subtle seasoning. He also notices that Adam uses the term *guardrails*, which is otherwise given to an AI agent, and considers it an accurate concept: someone must define the boundaries for each area.

David asks how Praktika achieves that balance in practice. Are social media and growth allowed to be completely unhinged, or is there an upper limit there too, just higher than in the product?

Adam answers that the boundaries for the product are **very clear**. The team internally agreed on what they do and what they do not do, and all of that fits on **a single page of description** because it does not need to be complicated. In the growth area, influencers are left to do their job. There are some basic constraints, but the difference according to Adam's words is very large. True to their principle, they allow influencers to come up with almost any approach they want.

sections.subtitle: 50 milijuna ARR-a s nešto više od 40 ljudi
sections.screenshot_description: Adam Turaev iznosi trenutačne brojke: 50 milijuna dolara ARR-a i gotovo pola milijuna pretplatnika
sections.content:
Pred kraj razgovora David pita gdje je Praktika danas, nakon skoka s jednog na dvanaest milijuna ARR-a, i kako izgleda tim.

Adam iznosi brojke:

- **50 milijuna dolara ARR-a**,
- **gotovo pola milijuna pretplatnika koji plaćaju**,
- **nešto više od 40 zaposlenih**,
- prihod po zaposleniku **veći od milijun dolara**.

David reagira kratkim „Wow“. Adam naglašava da je tim i dalje vrlo malen.
sections.subtitle_en: 50 Million ARR with Just Over 40 People
sections.screenshot_description_en: Adam Turaev Presents Current Figures: 50 Million Dollars in ARR and Nearly Half a Million Subscribers
sections.content_en:
Toward the end of the conversation, David asks where Praktika is today, after the jump from one to twelve million ARR, and what the team looks like.

Adam presents the figures:

- **50 million dollars ARR**,
- **nearly half a million paying subscribers**,
- **just over 40 employees**,
- revenue per employee **greater than one million dollars**.

David reacts with a brief “Wow.” Adam emphasizes that the team is still very small.

sections.subtitle: Proaktivni AI coachevi: AI koji vodi čovjeka, a ne radi umjesto njega
sections.screenshot_description: Adam Turaev objašnjava razliku između AI-ja koji obavlja zadatke i AI-ja koji vodi i poboljšava korisnika
sections.content:
Adam kaže da je trenutačni fokus učiniti AI coacheve **proaktivnijima**. Učenje je bolan proces, pa bi coachevi trebali aktivno voditi korisnika. Inspiraciju pronalazi u onome što rade **Muse** i **Dots**. Jacob primjećuje da je *harness engineering* očito postao važna tema.

Adam objašnjava čime se Praktika razlikuje. Mnogi AI alati su, kako ih naziva, *accomplisher AI*: obavljaju zadatke umjesto korisnika. Praktika želi voditi i poboljšavati korisnika kao osobu. Prema njegovim riječima, kvaliteta izlaza ovisi o kvaliteti ulaza, pa tvrtka radi upravo na ulazu, odnosno na tome da ljudi alate koriste ispravno.

To povezuje i sa sigurnošću umjetne inteligencije. Smatra da je za siguran AI važno tko ga koristi, kako je ta osoba educirana i s kojim pristupom koristi alate. Misiju Praktike u tom ekosustavu vidi u izgradnji coacheva koji ljudima pomažu da napreduju. Počeli su s učenjem jezika, ali planiraju se **proširiti i na druge predmete**.

Jacob u tome vidi primjer agentne verzije tradicionalne kategorije aplikacija. Praktika je krenula od izravnog pristupa: razgovor, rečenica, reakcija. Problem se, međutim, brzo proširuje na sve ono na čemu aplikacije rade desetljećima, poput nizova uzastopnih dana učenja (*streaks*), zadržavanja korisnika i povratka u aplikaciju. Pretpostavlja da će sve više toga prepustiti agentu.

Adam potvrđuje da to već rade. Za postavljanje dnevnog podsjetnika aplikacija ne nudi klasično sučelje, nego tutor sam pita korisnika želi li podsjetnik i ponudi da ga postavi. Adam tako zamišlja budućnost. Jacob napominje da će to imati zanimljive posljedice za mjerenje i testiranje proizvoda jer se svaki agent ponaša malo drukčije.
sections.subtitle_en: Proactive AI Coaches: AI That Guides the Human Rather Than Working for Them
sections.screenshot_description_en: Adam Turaev Explains the Difference Between AI That Performs Tasks and AI That Guides and Improves the User
sections.content_en:
Adam says that the current focus is to make AI coaches **more proactive**. Learning is a painful process, so coaches should actively guide the user. He finds inspiration in what **Muse** and **Dots** are doing. Jacob remarks that *harness engineering* has clearly become an important topic.

Adam explains how Praktika differs. Many AI tools are, as he calls them, *accomplisher AI*: they perform tasks instead of the user. Praktika wants to guide and improve the user as a person. According to him, the quality of the output depends on the quality of the input, so the company is working precisely on the input, that is, on having people use the tools properly.

He connects this with artificial intelligence safety as well. He believes that for safe AI, it matters who uses it, how that person is educated, and with what mindset they use the tools. He sees Praktika's mission in that ecosystem in building coaches that help people advance. They started with language learning, but they plan to **expand to other subjects as well**.

Jacob sees in this an example of an agentic version of a traditional app category. Praktika started from a direct approach: conversation, sentence, reaction. The problem, however, quickly expands to everything apps have been working on for decades, such as learning streaks (*streaks*), user retention, and returning to the app. He assumes that more and more of that will be handed over to the agent.

Adam confirms that they are already doing that. To set a daily reminder, the app does not offer a classic interface, but the tutor itself asks the user whether they want a reminder and offers to set it. That is how Adam envisions the future. Jacob notes that this will have interesting implications for product measurement and testing because each agent behaves slightly differently.

sections.subtitle: Prvo kvaliteta, a modeli će pojeftiniti: ekonomika inferencije
sections.screenshot_description: Adam Turaev objašnjava zašto daje prednost kvaliteti pred troškovima inferencije i ističe da je Praktika profitabilna
sections.content:
David otvara pitanje koje danas muči mnoge osnivače. Granični trošak više nije nula, pa ga zanima kako Praktika uravnotežuje troškove generiranja avatara, razgovora uživo i inferencije s cijenom pretplate i freemium modelom. Jacob dodaje kvalitetu kao treći čimbenik jer se čini da su trošak inferencije i kvaliteta usko povezani: bolja kvaliteta zahtijeva skuplju inferenciju.

Adam je jasan: uvijek mu je fokus na **najboljoj kvaliteti za korisnike** jer se to dugoročno isplati. Modeli s vremenom postaju sve jeftiniji, pa će ta ekonomija sama doći na svoje. Kao primjer navodi nedavna izdanja modela koji se u transkriptu naziva **Luna**. Verzija 5.6 bila je **oko 50 % jeftinija**, pa je tim odmah zaključio da im se ekonomija popravila. Dva do tri tjedna kasnije stigla je **Luna 6**, ponovno **50 % jeftinija** od već pojeftinjenog prethodnika.

Adam usput naglašava da je **Praktika profitabilna**. Prema njegovim riječima, na ovoj se razini može biti profitabilan i nastaviti rasti bez spaljivanja novca. Ne poručuje da treba prikupljati kapital i trošiti ga samo radi kvalitete, nego da se kvaliteta i učinkovitost mogu uskladiti.

Jacob ne vidi granicu tom pojeftinjenju, s obzirom na gradnju podatkovnih centara. Smatra i da u nekom trenutku tutor postane „dovoljno pametan“. Njemu treba prilično inteligentan tutor španjolskog, a ne superinteligencija koja rješava Navier-Stokesove probleme. Adam se nadovezuje šalom o tutoru koji podučava španjolski i usput pomaže graditi raketu. Jacob zaključuje da tada više ne treba pratiti krivulju inteligencije, nego model proglasiti dovoljno dobrim, a cijena bi trebala padati.
sections.subtitle_en: Quality first, and models will get cheaper: the economics of inference
sections.screenshot_description_en: Adam Turaev explains why he prioritizes quality over inference costs and highlights that Praktika is profitable
sections.content_en:
David opens a question that troubles many founders today. The marginal cost is no longer zero, so he is interested in how Praktika balances the costs of avatar generation, live conversation, and inference with subscription pricing and the freemium model. Jacob adds quality as a third factor because inference cost and quality seem closely linked: better quality requires more expensive inference.

Adam is clear: his focus is always on **the best quality for users** because that pays off in the long run. Over time, models become increasingly cheaper, so those economics will fall into place on their own. As an example, he cites recent releases of the model referred to in the transcript as **Luna**. Version 5.6 was **about 50% cheaper**, so the team immediately concluded that their economics had improved. Two to three weeks later, **Luna 6** arrived, once again **50% cheaper** than its already discounted predecessor.

Along the way, Adam emphasizes that **Praktika is profitable**. According to him, at this level one can be profitable and continue to grow without burning money. He is not saying that one should raise capital and spend it solely for the sake of quality, but rather that quality and efficiency can be aligned.

Jacob sees no limit to this cheapening, considering the construction of data centers. He also believes that at some point a tutor becomes "smart enough." He needs a reasonably intelligent Spanish tutor, not a superintelligence that solves Navier-Stokes problems. Adam follows up with a joke about a tutor who teaches Spanish and along the way helps build a rocket. Jacob concludes that at that point one no longer needs to follow the intelligence curve, but rather declare the model good enough, and the price should drop.

sections.subtitle: Modeli na uređaju i AI jeftin poput baze podataka
sections.screenshot_description: Adam Turaev iznosi svoju okladu da će krajnji ishod biti modeli koji rade izravno na uređaju
sections.content:
Adam iznosi svoju okladu za dugoročnu budućnost: krajnji ishod bit će modeli koji **u cijelosti rade na samom uređaju**. Jacob se nadovezuje da se tako računalna snaga distribuira na uređaje.

Kao drugi mogući scenarij Jacob navodi da će AI postati jeftin kao baze podataka. RevenueCat ima vrlo velike i skupe baze, ali o njima nitko ne razmišlja kao o skupom AI-ju jer se baze podataka optimiziraju već četrdeset godina i stalno pojeftinjuju. Vjeruje da će se isto dogoditi s umjetnom inteligencijom: cijena će padati sve dok granični trošak na velikoj razini ne postane cijena kilovata potrebnog za njezin rad.
sections.subtitle_en: On-device models and AI as cheap as a database
sections.screenshot_description_en: Adam Turaev shares his bet that the ultimate outcome will be models running directly on-device
sections.content_en:
Adam presents his bet for the long-term future: the ultimate outcome will be models that **run entirely on the device itself**. Jacob adds that in this way computing power is distributed to devices.

As another possible scenario, Jacob states that AI will become as cheap as databases. RevenueCat has very large and expensive databases, but no one thinks of them as expensive AI because databases have been optimized for forty years and are constantly getting cheaper. He believes the same will happen with artificial intelligence: the price will fall until the marginal cost at scale becomes the price of the kilowatt needed for its operation.

sections.subtitle: Najveći uspjeh godine: odlazak s Fluttera na nativni iOS
sections.screenshot_description: Adam Turaev otkriva da je prelazak s Fluttera na nativni iOS bio najveći uspjeh godine
sections.content:
Na kraju David postavlja tri pitanja koja postavlja svakom gostu. Prvo je koji je eksperiment ili promjena u prošloj godini imao najveći učinak.

Adamov odgovor iznenađuje: najveći uspjeh bio je **prelazak s višeplatformskog Fluttera na nativni iOS**. Ni tim to nije očekivao. Kako kaže, uglavnom su se molili da ne izgube metrike na kojima su godinama radili. Prelazak je stabilizirao aplikaciju i korisnicima donio najbolje moguće iskustvo na njihovim uređajima. To se isplatilo **poboljšanjem praktički svih metrika**, od konverzijskih do metrika angažmana. Jacob to opisuje kao osjećaj da je aplikacija postala „čvršća“.

Na Jacobovo pitanje je li razvoj sada brži, Adam odgovara da nije bitno drukčiji. Tim je i prije bio brz i provodio mnogo eksperimenata.

Jacob iznosi širu analizu. U ranim fazama AI revolucije činilo se da su Flutter i React Native važniji nego ikad jer su agenti bili bolji u tim tehnologijama. Vrlo brzo se, međutim, pokazalo da agent može pisati nativni iOS i nativni Android, pa je izbor tehnologije gotovo postao implementacijski detalj. Dodaje da je Flutter imao i neke dizajnerske odluke zbog kojih se slabije uklapa u novi svijet nego čak React Native.

Adam priznaje da Flutter i dalje obavlja posao i omogućuje da se jednim potezom pokriju dvije platforme. Ipak, kad bi kretao ispočetka, prvo bi napravio nativni iOS, a zatim Android. Jacob se šali da je dovoljno uzeti pretplatu Claude Max Pro, dati agentu Codex obje aplikacije i reći mu da ih pretvori „bez pogrešaka“. David to zaključuje ironičnim „Toliko je jednostavno, Jacobe“.
sections.subtitle_en: The year's biggest success: moving from Flutter to native iOS
sections.screenshot_description_en: Adam Turaev reveals that switching from Flutter to native iOS was the biggest success of the year
sections.content_en:
At the end, David asks the three questions he asks every guest. The first is which experiment or change in the past year had the greatest impact.

Adam's answer is surprising: the greatest success was the **transition from cross-platform Flutter to native iOS**. Even the team did not expect that. As he says, they were mostly praying that they wouldn't lose the metrics they had worked on for years. The transition stabilized the app and brought users the best possible experience on their devices. That paid off with **an improvement in practically all metrics**, from conversion to engagement metrics. Jacob describes that as a feeling that the application became "tighter."

To Jacob's question of whether development is now faster, Adam replies that it is not significantly different. The team was fast before as well and conducted many experiments.

Jacob presents a broader analysis. In the early stages of the AI revolution, it seemed that Flutter and React Native were more important than ever because agents were better at those technologies. Very quickly, however, it turned out that an agent can write native iOS and native Android, so the choice of technology almost became an implementation detail. He adds that Flutter also had some design decisions that make it fit less well into the new world than even React Native.

Adam admits that Flutter still gets the job done and allows covering two platforms in a single stroke. Still, if he were starting from scratch, he would build native iOS first, and then Android. Jacob jokes that it is enough to get a Claude Max Pro subscription, give the Codex agent both apps, and tell it to convert them "without errors." David concludes that with an ironic "It's that simple, Jacob."

sections.subtitle: Najveći promašaj, kopije konkurencije i poziv „ludim ljudima“
sections.screenshot_description: Adam Turaev najavljuje otvorena radna mjesta u Praktici i zahvaljuje voditeljima
sections.content:
Na pitanje o najvećem promašaju prošle godine Adam bez oklijevanja ponovno spominje **„unhinged“ avatare**. Jacob se šali o „trajnoj šteti za brend“. David pojašnjava da su ti avatari uvedeni u aplikaciju, gdje su uznemirili ljude i pokvarili im iskustvo. Adam dodaje da se korisnicima jednostavno nisu svidjeli. Smatra da je to vjerojatno specifično za Praktiku jer je njezina slika na tržištu više slika „dobrih momaka“, pa takvi avatari nisu prošli.

Posljednje pitanje glasi: rast bi bio lakši kada... Adam odgovara kratko: **kada ne bi bilo kopija konkurencije**. Jacob se šali da svi zapravo žele biti monopolisti i dodaje da je „konkurencija za gubitnike“.

Za kraj David pita želi li Adam nešto poručiti ili najaviti otvorena radna mjesta. Praktika trenutačno traži:

- **web inženjera**,
- **voditelja akvizicije korisnika** (*user acquisition manager*).

Adam poručuje da tvrtka traži „lude ljude“ spremne raditi 24 sata dnevno, sedam dana u tjednu kako bi osvojili ovo tržište, i poziva takve kandidate da se jave. Zahvaljuje na razgovoru, koji mu je bio vrlo zabavan. David i Jacob mu uzvraćaju zahvalom.
sections.subtitle_en: The biggest failure, competitor copies, and an invitation to "crazy people"
sections.screenshot_description_en: Adam Turaev announces open positions at Praktika and thanks the hosts
sections.content_en:
When asked about the biggest failure of the past year, Adam without hesitation mentions the **"unhinged" avatars** again. Jacob jokes about "permanent brand damage." David clarifies that those avatars were introduced into the app, where they disturbed people and ruined their experience. Adam adds that the users simply did not like them. He believes that this is probably specific to Praktika because its market image is more of a "nice guys" image, so such avatars did not succeed.

The final question is: growth would be easier if... Adam answers briefly: **if there were no competitor copies**. Jacob jokes that everyone actually wants to be a monopolist and adds that "competition is for losers."

In closing, David asks if Adam wants to share any message or announce open positions. Praktika is currently looking for:

- a **web engineer**,
- a **user acquisition manager** (*user acquisition manager*).

Adam shares that the company is looking for "crazy people" ready to work 24 hours a day, seven days a week to conquer this market, and invites such candidates to reach out. He thanks them for the conversation, which was very fun for him. David and Jacob return the thanks.
